name: Pagination
hint: Page with ← →: the pill slides and the numbers glide; hover … to jump several pages.
description: Page numbers with gaps that stay readable. The current page sits on a pill that slides to the new page while the numbers glide into their new slots, and the control keeps a constant width so nothing moves under the pointer. Hovering a gap turns it into a multi-page jump. A compact layout rolls the page number.
usage: Use when people need to reach a specific page or share a page link. Pass the number of pages as `count` (or `total` items with `pageSize`), own the page with `page` + `onPageChange(page)`, and set `busy` while the next page loads. Pass `getHref(page)` when pages have URLs, so every page is a real link. For feeds people only scroll forward through, use infinite loading with a Load more button instead.

keyboard.does: Moves through previous, each page, the … jumps and next; a disabled arrow is skipped.

Goes to the focused page, to the page before or after, or jumps several pages; when the pressed control goes away or turns disabled, focus moves to the new current page (in the compact layout, to the arrow still enabled).
Goes to the previous or next page and focuses it.
Goes to the first or last page and focuses it.

screenReader: A nav landmark named by `ariaLabel` ("Pagination" by default). Each page button is named "Page N" (`labels.page`) and the current one carries aria-current="page"; the arrows are "Previous page" and "Next page", natively disabled at the ends, and each … is named "Jump forward 5 pages" or "Jump back 5 pages". While `busy` the nav is aria-busy; the caption line and the compact "Page N of M" are polite live regions.

dataProps.description: Controlled current page (1-based). Pass with onPageChange.
(page, event) => void when the user picks a page (number, previous / next, a … jump, arrow keys, Home / End). With getHref the event is the link click, so a router can preventDefault.
Number of pages. Wins over total.
With pageSize: the number of items (pages = ceil(total / pageSize)). Without pageSize: the number of pages.
Items per page; turns total into an item count and gives caption its from / to.
(page) => URL. Every page, previous / next and jump becomes an <a href>; unavailable ends are aria-disabled links with no href.
Every control inert and out of the tab order.
You are loading a page: the nav is aria-busy and nothing fires until you clear it.

dataProps.type: node | ((info: { page: number; count: number; from?: number; to?: number; total?: number }) => node)
dataProps.description: Line under the control: a node, or ({ page, count, from, to, total }) => node (from / to / total need pageSize).

dataProps.type: Partial<{ previous: string; next: string; first: string; last: string; page: (page: number) => string; jumpBack: (pages: number) => string; jumpForward: (pages: number) => string; compact: node; of: node }>
dataProps.description: Accessible names and compact text, merged over { previous: "Previous page", next: "Next page", first: "First page", last: "Last page", page: (p) => `Page ${p}`, jumpBack: (n) => …, jumpForward: (n) => …, compact: "Page", of: "of" }.
Accessible name of the nav landmark.
How the pages are shown between previous and next: "numbers" is the row of page buttons with a sliding pill and … jumps, "compact" is one line ("Page 7 of 24") whose number rolls.

Height of each page button: sm 30px (under a dense table), md 36px, lg 44px (beside 52px buttons); the bar adds 4px around them. On a touch screen every size is at least 44px, and on a narrow row buttons shrink before neighbours drop. A number sets it in px exactly.
Any other attribute (id, aria-*, data-*) goes to the root <div>. className and style are merged with the component's own.
